item.title: Downtown Board Backs Traditional Mardi Gras Route, But Wants More Data First
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola's Downtown Improvement Board has signaled support for returning the city's Mardi Gras parades to their historic route, but stopped short of a final vote pending additional information, according to WKRG-TV 5. The board's cautious approach suggests the decision involves weighing multiple factors — likely including traffic impact, public…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's Downtown Improvement Board has signaled support for returning the city's Mardi Gras parades to their historic route, but stopped short of a final vote pending additional information, according to WKRG-TV 5.

The board's cautious approach suggests the decision involves weighing multiple factors — likely including traffic impact, public safety, business concerns, and logistical considerations for parade organizers. The traditional route represents a return to how Pensacola has historically celebrated Mardi Gras, a major draw for the city's Carnival season.

No timeline for a final decision was announced. The board is expected to gather and review the additional details before moving forward with a formal recommendation or vote on the parade route.

item.title: Taddeo Attacks Ingoglia's $3.7M in State-Funded Ads as Election Nears
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic CFO candidate Annette Taddeo is calling out Republican incumbent Blaise Ingoglia for what she characterizes as misuse of taxpayer money on advertising featuring his name and image ahead of the November election. According to reporting by journalist Jason Garcia reviewed by Taddeo's campaign, the Florida Department of Financial Services…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic CFO candidate Annette Taddeo is calling out Republican incumbent Blaise Ingoglia for what she characterizes as misuse of taxpayer money on advertising featuring his name and image ahead of the November election. According to reporting by journalist Jason Garcia reviewed by Taddeo's campaign, the Florida Department of Financial Services has spent more than $3.7 million on advertising since July, with more than $2.3 million of that spending occurring in just the last three weeks.

The ads, which promote hurricane preparedness, unclaimed property recovery, and senior fraud prevention, prominently feature Ingoglia's name, photo, and biography. Taddeo argues the spending mirrors the "Hope Florida" scandal that resulted in a grand jury finding that $10 million in Medicaid settlement funds were misappropriated through what investigators called a "sophisticated scheme to fund political activities." She noted that one of the firms producing the current ads was previously hired by the DeSantis administration during that earlier controversy.

According to recent polling cited by Taddeo's campaign, the CFO race is tightly competitive, with both candidates polling at 42 percent. Taddeo, a Democrat, leads among no-party-affiliation voters. Despite Ingoglia's role as CFO overseeing state finances, Taddeo said he has not launched an investigation into the advertising spending. She's also raised questions about more than $500,000 in taxpayer-funded legal fees for Ingoglia's chief of staff, Katie Strickland, who was involved in events examined by the Hope Florida grand jury.

item.title: County Library Leadership Fight Draws Sustained Public Heat
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Seven months into a dispute over West Florida Public Libraries leadership, residents continue to keep the pressure on Escambia County commissioners, contradicting County Administrator Wes Moreno's repeated prediction that public interest would fade within two weeks. According to InWeekly, Moreno has consistently assured commissioners that the…
item.content:encoded:
Seven months into a dispute over West Florida Public Libraries leadership, residents continue to keep the pressure on Escambia County commissioners, contradicting County Administrator Wes Moreno's repeated prediction that public interest would fade within two weeks.

According to InWeekly, Moreno has consistently assured commissioners that the library director controversy would blow over quickly and that most residents wouldn't care about the outcome. But sustained citizen attendance at county commission meetings and continued public engagement suggest otherwise.

The library leadership question has become one of the longer-running public controversies at the county level, with community members showing up regularly to voice their concerns. The persistence of the issue underscores how library services—and who runs them—matter to a significant segment of the Escambia County population, particularly among those who use or care about public library resources.

item.title: Pensacola Ballet explores loss and humanity in new 'Frankenstein' ballet
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola Ballet is preparing to stage a new interpretation of "Frankenstein" that centers on the emotional and relational dimensions of Mary Shelley's classic novel, according to reporting by InWeekly. Choreographer Gonzalo Galguera is directing the production, which reimagines the gothic tale through a focus on human connection and grief. In…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Ballet is preparing to stage a new interpretation of "Frankenstein" that centers on the emotional and relational dimensions of Mary Shelley's classic novel, according to reporting by InWeekly.

Choreographer Gonzalo Galguera is directing the production, which reimagines the gothic tale through a focus on human connection and grief. In recent rehearsals at the company's third-floor studio, Galguera has been working with dancers on the final scene—one in which Victor Frankenstein stands beside his dying father while the Creature looms over both men.

Rather than simply running through steps, Galguera is grounding the performers in the emotional reality of the moment. Before asking dancers to move through the scene, he talks them through what it means to lose a parent, helping them access the vulnerability and depth that the moment demands. That approach underscores the ballet's ambition to treat the story as deeply human—not merely spectacle, but an exploration of connection, responsibility, and the cost of creation.

item.content:encoded: With the 2026 General Election approaching, Escambia County voters have until October 5 to register or confirm their voter registration status. According to InWeekly, even if you believe you're already registered, election officials recommend verifying your status at vote.gov—a process that takes less than a minute. The deadline applies to all Florida voters, including those in Santa Rosa County and the broader Northwest Florida region. Checking your registration now can help prevent any last-minute surprises on Election Day.

item.title: Eglin Federal Credit Union honors Mary Calvert's 25 years of service
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Eglin Federal Credit Union celebrated a major milestone Tuesday when Information Systems Core Systems Computer Operator II Mary Calvert was recognized for 25 years with the organization. The Fort Walton Beach resident began her career at Eglin FCU on August 31, 2001, as a full-time teller at the Hurlburt Field Branch, where she spent more than two…
item.content:encoded:
Eglin Federal Credit Union celebrated a major milestone Tuesday when Information Systems Core Systems Computer Operator II Mary Calvert was recognized for 25 years with the organization. The Fort Walton Beach resident began her career at Eglin FCU on August 31, 2001, as a full-time teller at the Hurlburt Field Branch, where she spent more than two decades providing member services.

Calvert's career path reflects steady advancement within the credit union. In July 2022, she transitioned to the Information Systems Department as a Computer/Imaging Operator at the Fort Walton Beach Branch. She earned a promotion to IS Core Systems Computer Operator I in August 2025, followed by another promotion to IS Core Systems Computer Operator II just one month later.

"Your hard work, positive attitude and willingness to support others have made a lasting impact on both our members and your coworkers," Information Systems Manager Susan Coup said at a celebratory breakfast held at the Operations Center. Calvert is set to retire on January 4, 2027.

Reflecting on her quarter-century with the organization, Calvert expressed gratitude for the relationships and opportunities she experienced. "Eglin FCU has provided me with meaningful opportunities, lasting friendships and a strong sense of purpose throughout my career," she said.

item.title: Free neighborhood cleanup coming to Bellview East on Oct. 7
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County is bringing a free neighborhood cleanup to the Bellview East area on Wednesday, October 7, giving residents a chance to dispose of bulky items and household waste at no cost. Residents in the designated cleanup zone who received a postcard with details can place eligible items at the curb by 7 a.m. on cleanup day. The county will…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is bringing a free neighborhood cleanup to the Bellview East area on Wednesday, October 7, giving residents a chance to dispose of bulky items and household waste at no cost.

Residents in the designated cleanup zone who received a postcard with details can place eligible items at the curb by 7 a.m. on cleanup day. The county will haul away old appliances, electronics, furniture, mattresses, yard debris, bicycles, grills, and household hazardous waste like paint, motor oil, and batteries. Tires are accepted up to 10 per household.

Some items won't be collected, including building materials like concrete and lumber, auto parts, dirt, vehicles, and explosives. Only residents within the targeted cleanup area are eligible to participate, and items left outside that zone won't be picked up.

The Escambia County Community Redevelopment Agency runs these periodic neighborhood cleanups across the county. For questions about the Oct. 7 event, residents can contact the CRA at 850-595-3217 or cra@myescambia.com.

item.title: City of Pensacola Reschedules Selection Committee Meetings for Hospital Campus Demolition Project
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Pensacola has rescheduled two selection committee meetings related to the demolition of the former Baptist Hospital campus on the South side. According to a city announcement, the first meeting—originally planned for September 22—will now be held October 6 at 10 a.m. at City Hall, 222 W. Main St., in the Hagler-Mason Conference Room on…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola has rescheduled two selection committee meetings related to the demolition of the former Baptist Hospital campus on the South side.

According to a city announcement, the first meeting—originally planned for September 22—will now be held October 6 at 10 a.m. at City Hall, 222 W. Main St., in the Hagler-Mason Conference Room on the second floor. That session will distribute materials and review guidelines for committee members overseeing the Request for Proposals (RFP 26-053) for a decommissioning and demolition contractor. The meeting is open to the public.

A second selection committee meeting to shortlist firms for interviews or presentations has been moved from October 6 to October 20 at 10 a.m., also at City Hall. That meeting will take place in the Whibbs Conference Room on the first floor.

The project involves demolition work at the South Former Baptist Hospital Campus, which is located in a Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) area.

item.content:encoded:
Jim Allen Elementary School has rescheduled its fall carnival due to an unfavorable weather forecast for this Friday. The event will now take place Friday, November 6, from 3 to 6 p.m.

Wristbands for the carnival will be available for purchase from November 2 through November 5 at $10 each. The school says all wristbands sold before the original date will be honored at the rescheduled event, so families who already bought tickets don't need to purchase new ones.

Parents and students looking for more details about the carnival activities and pricing can contact the school directly.

item.content:encoded: The Century Town Council unanimously approved a lower property tax rate and the town's $8.48 million budget during a brief meeting Tuesday afternoon. The lower rate comes as the small North Escambia community continues to manage its finances amid broader economic pressures facing municipal governments across the region.

item.title: Testimony begins in trial of ex-deputy charged in airman's death
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A courtroom packed with supporters of Roger Fortson heard the opening of testimony Wednesday in the case against former Okaloosa County Deputy Eddie Duran, who is charged in connection with the death of the Air Force airman. Fortson, stationed at nearby NAS Pensacola, was shot in May 2023 during a welfare check at his Fort Walton Beach home. The…
item.content:encoded:
A courtroom packed with supporters of Roger Fortson heard the opening of testimony Wednesday in the case against former Okaloosa County Deputy Eddie Duran, who is charged in connection with the death of the Air Force airman.

Fortson, stationed at nearby NAS Pensacola, was shot in May 2023 during a welfare check at his Fort Walton Beach home. The case has drawn significant community attention and support for Fortson's family.

Duran, a former member of the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office, faces charges stemming from the shooting. The trial is underway in Okaloosa County, which borders Santa Rosa County to the west of Escambia.
